summary: Kathleen Kenyon (1906–1978) was an archaeologist and historian. Educated at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College, she held appointments at the University of London (~1935–1962), the UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017), where she served as Associate Professor of Religion.

Kathleen McDonald (b. 1952) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned degrees from Juniata College and the University of Michigan (PhD under Walter M. Spink, and MD), completed residency at University of Utah Hospital, and joined the University of Utah in 2024.

Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held academic posts at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 1998) and the University of Manitoba (attested 1999).

Katia Buffetrille (b. 1948) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her degrees from Paris Nanterre University, studying under Alexander W. Macdonald, and held positions at the CRCAO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the journal EMSCAT.

Katia Chirkova specializes in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied at Beijing Language and Culture University and Leiden University (PhD), subsequently holding research posts at Leiden University (2003–2005), IIAS (2005–2006), and the Centre de Recherches Linguistiques sur l'Asie Orientale (2006).

Katja Triplett (b. 1965) is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Marburg. She has held teaching and research appointments at Marburg, SOAS, Basel, Birkbeck, Munich, Göttingen, Hannover, and Leipzig.

Katragadda Paddayya (b. 1943) is an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. After completing his doctoral studies at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1968), he served as a professor and Professor of Geo-archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1970–2008).

Katrin Querl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Munich, Kagyu College, and the University of Vienna (Dr. phil.), and has held academic posts at the University of Leipzig and the University of Hamburg.

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and served at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Doshisha University (~1964–1968), he served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1998–2016).

Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) was a Japanese linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita (1874–1946) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1893 to 1896 and held a post there from ~1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki (b. 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University, INALCO, and the University of Paris under Gadjin Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, he served as a professor at Kyoto University.

Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1973) and served as a professor, director, and professor emeritus at Hanazono University between ~1985 and 2014.

Katsumi Tanabe (b. 1941) is a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1973) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–1999) and Chuo University (~1999–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist. He earned his degrees from Kyoto University, holding posts there, at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kansai University, Nara National Museum, and Ryukoku University.

Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was an art historian and Indologist educated at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and Panjab University. She held posts at Marg Publications, the College of Art, NIT Delhi, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
